title: Reinforcement learning allocates COVID-19 border tests to travelers in Greece
summary: The reinforcement learning system Eva allocated Greece's limited testing resources across all borders in summer 2020 using travelers' demographics and earlier test results. Against modeled counterfactuals it identified 1.85 times as many asymptomatic infected travelers as random testing (2-4 times at peak) and 1.25-1.45 times as many as policies based on epidemiological metrics. Comparators are counterfactual estimates rather than randomized controls; this is a version 1 SSRN preprint abstract.
ai_technology: Reinforcement learning system (Eva) allocating tests to arriving travelers and estimating prevalence

evidence.tested: Real deployment at Greek borders compared with modeled counterfactual policies; classified as retrospective or benchmark because comparisons are counterfactual.
evidence.unknown: Comparison against randomized testing, other countries and later pandemic phases; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Decides whom to test and estimates prevalence in real time.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
